cheer.head: What you pulled off · three things you can say out loud
s2.title: Opening move
s2.note: Ask whether it can be done, before asking how
s2.daysNote: Each bar = tool calls that day, scaled to the busiest day. {detail}
s3.title: Turn spectrum
s3.noteOne: 1 session · each bar is one turn
s3.noteMany: {n} sessions · each bar is one turn
s3.lede: Bar height is how many tools that turn used; colour is the quality score: greener is smoother, redder is a crash. The shape is front-loaded — the first two days ate {share}% of the work ({two} of {tools} calls); everything after was polishing.
s3.lgWrote: Cyan cap = this turn wrote files
s3.qnote: q is computed, not judged by a model: base 70, +10 for a successful file write, −12 per tool error, −10 if the turn was interrupted, +8 if you carried on the next turn, −12 if you changed direction. It measures whether the turn moved the project forward and whether it left debt behind — not how you felt about it.
s3.picksNote: Click a card to see what was actually said
s4.title: Decision ledger
s4.note: {n} forks · open one to see the comparison and what came of it
s4.lede: Each node is one moment where the AI proposed something and you either took it or rewrote it on the spot. The dashed line on the left is what it wanted; the solid line on the right is the road you actually took. Open a node for the comparison, then what the next 3 turns produced — all counted from the log, none of it invented.
s5.title: Rework analysis
s5.lede: Rework is not the same as editing a lot. A file touched ten times may just be a requirement still growing. Only one thing counts here: the previous version was judged unusable and had to be redone. Each episode quotes what you actually said — the cause and the prescription were written after reading those words, not guessed from edit counts.
s5.hotNote: not rework — just where the weight landed
s6.title: How you show up in a project
s7.title: Your rule library
s7.lede: This is not a summary — it is something you can hand to the next AI. Uncheck what you disagree with, pick where to install it, and the text below follows. Copy it, or download it as AGENTS.md.
s7.hint: Takes effect in the next session you start. Existing content is not overwritten; repeated sections are merged.
s8.title: Coach page · if you ran it again
s8.note: Three items, each pinned to a number
s8.lede: The celebration page says what you achieved; this one says what you could save next time. None of it is "practise more" — every item points at specific turns in the log.
ft.source: Source: DeepSeek Harness session logs · {turns} turns / {tools} tool calls / {errors} errors
ft.note: Numbers computed by scripts; narrative written by a model · inferences are marked
ask.title: The one time it was your call
ask.q: T{turn} — I gave you {n} options and asked: {q}
deg.title: This report comes from Claude Code logs.
deg.body: Those logs carry no todos, approvals or background jobs — so “how many approvals”, “how many open todos”, “how long did a job run” are absent from this page, not zero.
tg.dsh.d: ~/.dsh/AGENTS.md · read on every DSH request, applies to all projects
tg.agents.d: ~/.agents/AGENTS.md · Claude Code / Codex read this one too
tg.none.d: Just copy it — I decide where it goes
s6.instrShort: you mostly speak in half sentences (“go on”, “that works”)
s6.instrShortPaste: , with the occasional ten-thousand-character log pasted in
s6.instrLong: you state the whole requirement up front
s6.instrLongPaste: , the longest being {k}k characters (a pasted log or code)
s6.instrEndLong: . Complete instructions, boundaries drawn in advance.
s6.pushBody: You reversed direction in the very next message {n} times. You rarely ask “what should I do”; you ask “is this right” — then answer it yourself.
s6.trustBody: Across {n} turns you let the AI offer options {ask} times. Everything else you decided outright.
s6.runA: You had it run things more often than it edited code — verification-driven, not description-driven.
s6.runB: More edits than runs — thinking by changing, confirming by rereading.
